snp1.6:3.2: The Thai edition has “duvijāno” (hard to know) here instead of “suvijāno” (easily known), but Thanissaro follows the reading that fits the sense of the verse and the Sutta Nipāta commentary’s explanation of it.
snp1.6:19.3: This line follows the Thai edition’s readings “padussati” and “dussati.” The PTS and Sri Lankan editions instead read “padissati”/“dissati,” giving the sense “he is seen,” rather than “he misbehaves/offends.”
